<reason>A more convincingly defended a bounded obligation: use existing retail infrastructure, preserve safety and recipient choice, and permit disposal after a genuine unsuccessful offer. B raised legitimate handling costs and a credible, more flexible disposal-charge alternative. However, its predicted losses in availability remained insufficiently weighed against cheaper food and avoided waste. A answered enforcement pressure directly and exposed B’s tendency to treat private profitability as a sufficient measure of social value.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s transfer question forced B to concede that lost full-price revenue is not itself a social loss. B correctly retained labor and availability concerns, but A’s closing sharply challenged the unsupported claim that expensive rescue was the typical case, narrowing the dispute to actual costs rather than lost margins.</best_rebuttal>
